transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-12-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Lead ML Eng - Aurora Labs), Liam O'Connor (CTO), Sara Ng (DevOps)

Summary: short discovery to understand Aurora Labs' use case and see if PLG quickstart makes sense, talk through time-to-first-token, credits, and next steps.
Topics: quickstart, free credits, pilot scope, security, latency/cost, dedicated/private options

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with Omar our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya: Doing good, thanks. Excited to learn about the quickstart, we want to see how fast we can get tokens flowing.
[00:14] Liam: Yeah, quick intro from our side — I'm Liam, CTO, Priya runs our ML infra and Sara handles platform.
[00:20] Sara: Hi all.
[00:22] Omar: Great. Quick agenda, we'll ask a few questions about your stack, then walk through the PLG quickstart flow — signup, free credits, time-to-first-token, then dig into security & deployment models.
[00:34] Priya: Sounds good. We mostly want hosted first, maybe dedicated later if we like perf and cost.
[00:40] Maya: That's common. Could you tell us current infra — cloud, k8s, any inference infra today?
[00:47] Priya: We're on GCP, services in GKE, model infra is a mix — some vect-db for embeddings, in-house LLM proxies for small tasks. We're testing retrieval-augmented generation w/ enterprise data.
[01:05] Liam: Main thing is latency under 300ms P95 for chat, and cost mid-term — want to understand unit economics.
[01:12] Omar: Understood. For PLG quickstart hosted, time-to-first-token is typically <10 minutes from signup: set API key, run quick example, generate first token. The free credits cover initial pilot workloads.
[01:28] Priya: Nice. What's in the quickstart — examples, SDK?
[01:32] Maya: We'll send a quickstart guide with code snippets (Python/Node), curl examples, and a sample dataset to try. Free credits get you X tokens (we'll include exact amount in the email).
[01:43] Sara: Any friction on network level? We can't expose some internal datasets publicly.
[01:48] Omar: For hosted you can redact or send synthetic samples for testing; for production private we offer VPC/private deployments and customer-managed KMS. Also Dedicated reserved capacity is an intermediate for isolation and throughput.
[02:05] Priya: For SOC2 and audit logs — do you have those?
[02:08] Maya: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II; we'll share the compliance pack and the audit log retention options.
[02:15] Liam: Good. Performance question — how does your runtime handle batching and KV cache? We saw mention of KV cache but docs were fuzzy.
[02:24] Omar: Our runtime does continuous batching and prefix/KV caching to improve CPU/GPU utilization. Sometimes the auto-transcript shows 'K-V cash' but it's KV cache — helps for repeated contexts to reduce tokens and latency.
[02:39] Priya: Do you support quantized model variants to reduce cost?
[02:42] Omar: Yes, we recommend quantized builds for cheaper deployments; Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles per workload. For hosted quickstart you'll test default models; we can run a cost/perf run to show tradeoffs.
[02:58] Maya: Quick question on SSO and RBAC — enterprise features — is SAML supported?
[03:02] Omar: Yes, SAML/SSO and RBAC are in our enterprise offering, we'll include docs.
[03:06] Priya: Timeline: we're hoping to evaluate in two weeks and decide on pilot by end of month.
[03:12] Maya: Good — quickstart fits that window. We'll provide free credits to run a pilot and Omar can hep with a tech session.
[03:19] Liam: For data residency — EU data center needs? We have EU customers and some data can't leave region.
[03:24] Maya: We have region routing and private options; for hosted we have region endpoints — Dedicated/Private lets you pin region or deploy on-prem. We'll send the region availability matrix.
[03:36] Sara: What about rate-limiting and quotas during pilot? If we run synthetic load, will we hit limits?
[03:41] Omar: We'll provision higher quotas for pilot; in quickstart we can unlock more tokens for testing.
[03:45] Priya: Can you share a performance benchmark for a similar company?
[03:49] Omar: Yes, I can share a 99th percentile latency sheet and a benchmarking spreadsheet — I'll attach it. Keep in mind results vary by sequence length and batch size.
[04:05] (background noise)
[04:12] Priya: A couple of clarifying points — 'time-to-first-token' we mean from API key to a streaming token, right?
[04:17] Maya: Correct. With SDK it's usually minutes. If you want a demo now, Omar can show a curl example.
[04:23] Omar: I can do a quick live demo but to save time I'll share a short recorded gif and the curl snippet.
[04:30] Liam: Ok. On cost, how does hosted billing look — per-token rates and embeddings?
[04:36] Maya: Hosted is usage-based per token and embeddings. For longer-term we can talk Reserved capacity for Dedicated to lower unit costs. We'll include a pricing summary.
[04:47] Priya: For security review, who do we talk to? We have a security questionnaire.
[04:51] Maya: We'll have our security lead review the questionnaire; send it to security@redwood.ai and we'll loop them in.
[05:00] Priya: Great. Any gotchas with redirected callbacks or webhooks?
[05:04] Omar: Standard TLS, and you can configure webhook endpoints; for private setups we can peer networks.
[05:09] Liam: If we do a POC with hosted, what's the path to move to Dedicated later? How disruptive?
[05:16] Omar: We provide the same API surface across hosted/dedicated/private. You can pin model versions and rollout policies; migration is largely configuration and capacity planning, not code changes.
[05:27] Priya: That reduces risk.
[05:29] (brief cross talk)
[05:35] Sara: Do you store customer prompts? Retention policies?
[05:38] Maya: For hosted we have configurable retention and can disable logging; for enterprise/private customers you control logs and retention via config/KMS. We'll include the retention matrix.
[05:49] Priya: Ok. One more — latency target 300ms P95, how realistic for <1k RPS?
[05:55] Omar: For that profile, hosted with smaller models or dedicated pools can meet 200-300ms P95. If you need lower, we can do dedicated hardware and tuning.
[06:07] Maya: Wrap up next steps: we'll send quickstart guide + credits, security docs, region matrix, and a benchmark sheet; Omar will run a baseline test if you share a small sample.
[06:18] Priya: Sounds good.
[06:20] Liam: Agreed.
[06:22] Maya: Any final questions?
[06:24] Priya: None here. We'll confirm pilot scope by Wednesday.
[06:28] Maya: Great — thanks everyone.
[06:30] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript: some names/words may be transcribed imperfectly (e.g., K-V cash -> KV cache), there are small filler words and interruptions. The real call included a brief demo follow-up not recorded in-line.

References/Links to share: quickstart guide (link in follow-up email), SOC2 pack (link), benchmarking spreadsheet (link), free credits redemption URL.
